title: HB450 (2021 Regular): Election Law – Polling Sites – Firearms Prohibitions

provenance.fetched_by: Open States bulk data (Maryland) (gun-policy Stage 5, Maryland); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Maryland text (First Reader; official copy, https://mgaleg.maryland.gov/2021RS/bills/hb/hb0450f.pdf)
provenance.note: first reader: bill as filed; no later version or vote was read. In 16–903(a)(3) the word [gun] was deleted from existing law and replaced by FIREARM.

operative_text:
Section 1 (Md. Code Ann., Election Law § 16–904(B)): EXCEPT AS PROVIDED IN § 16–903 OF THIS SUBTITLE, A PERSON MAY NOT: (1) CARRY OR DISPLAY A FIREARM ON THE PREMISES OF A PRIVATELY OR PUBLICLY OWNED BUILDING BEING USED AS A POLLING SITE DURING AN ELECTION, INCLUDING IN A PARKING LOT; OR (2) CARRY OR POSSESS A FIREARM WITHIN 100 FEET OF A POLLING SITE DURING AN ELECTION.
Section 1 (Md. Code Ann., Election Law § 16–904(C)): A PERSON WHO VIOLATES THIS SECTION IS SUBJECT TO THE CIVIL PENALTY SPECIFIED UNDER § 16–1002 OF THIS TITLE.
Section 1 (Md. Code Ann., Election Law § 16–903(a)(3)): except as required by law or by regulation adopted by the State Board in connection with ballot security activities, carrying or displaying a FIREARM, AS DEFINED IN § 16–904(A) OF THIS SUBTITLE, or badge within 100 feet of a polling site on election day.
Section 1 (Md. Code Ann., Election Law § 16–1002): A person who violates § 16–201(a)(6) or (7), § 16–903, OR § 16–904 of this title without knowing that the act is illegal shall pay a civil penalty and have the matter adjudicated in accordance with § 13–604 of this article.
